claim.qualifier: Rivian markets 'up to 28 mi of range per hour' on Level 2 home charging. The implied total time is rarely highlighted in marketing.
claim.verbatim_quote: gaining about 28 miles of range per hour

sources.name: Consumer Reports — 2025 Rivian R1S Road Test Report (citing manufacturer claim)

reality.qualifier: Consumer Reports measurement: ~15 hours to fully recharge the 140 kWh Max pack from empty on a 240V Level 2 home charger. Most US 240V residential circuits are sized at 40A continuous (9.6 kW); 28 mi/hr × 15 hr = 420 mi. For reference, a Tesla Model Y LR AWD charges in 12 hours; an F-150 Lightning ER in 14.6 hours.
reality.verbatim_quote: The huge 140-kilowatt-hour battery takes about 15 hours to recharge from empty on a 240-volt, Level 2 home-charging system, gaining about 28 miles of range per hour.

sources.name: Consumer Reports — 2025 Rivian R1S Road Test Report

narrative_one_liner: Rivian highlights '28 mi/hr' Level 2; the underlying full-charge time is ~15 hours (longest of major EVs).
narrative: Rivian's Level 2 home-charging marketing focuses on '28 mi/hr' — a number that sounds reasonable in isolation. The corresponding full-charge time on the 140 kWh Max battery is ~15 hours, longer than a single overnight charging window from low SOC. Buyers without an 80A continuous circuit (uncommon in US homes) will not be able to fully recharge an R1S Dual Max overnight after a low-battery day. This is not deception per se — the EPA-mandated 240V time is published — but the 28 mi/hr framing emphasizes a metric that minimizes the salience of the underlying limitation.
methodology_notes: Single Tier-2 source (CR). The mi/hr and hours-to-charge are mathematically equivalent given the battery size; the 'definitional' gap is in which framing the manufacturer chooses to highlight.
caveats: kind=definitional because both '28 mi/hr' and '15 hours' are correct facts about the same charging session. The deception is salience, not accuracy.

EPA-published 240V hours-to-charge is in our product file (12.0 hr for some R1S configurations on EPA, 15 hr per CR for the Max battery). Discrepancy may be due to circuit-amperage assumptions; investigate Phase 1.
alternative_explanations: Consumers may correctly interpret '28 mi/hr' as a per-hour rate; whether the framing is deceptive depends on whether buyers do the multiplication. Anecdotal evidence (forum posts) suggests many do not.
EPA mandates the 240V time disclosure; Rivian is not hiding the 15-hour number, only de-emphasizing it relative to the per-hour framing.
